semantic_correction.stem: A client receiving gastric enteral nutrition has a gastric residual volume of 350 mL and no nausea, vomiting, abdominal distention, or other signs of feeding intolerance. Which nursing interpretation is most appropriate?

options.A: Do not use the 350-mL residual by itself as an automatic reason to stop enteral nutrition; assess the client's overall tolerance and follow the prescribed or agency protocol.
options.B: Stop enteral nutrition because any residual above 200 mL confirms clinically significant intolerance, even when the client has no other gastrointestinal findings.
options.C: Increase the feeding rate to reduce the residual more quickly, because a moderate gastric residual indicates that additional formula will improve gastric emptying.
options.D: Base feeding-tolerance decisions primarily on the residual volume and disregard nausea, vomiting, distention, pain, bowel function, or other clinical findings.

semantic_correction.rationale: A is correct. Current NCBI/Open RN nursing guidance states that enteral nutrition should not be stopped for a gastric residual volume below 500 mL in the absence of other signs of intolerance because unnecessary interruption can reduce nutritional delivery. The same guidance directs nurses to assess for clinical findings such as abdominal bloating or distention, nausea, vomiting, cramping, diarrhea, and constipation and to follow agency policy for gastric-residual monitoring and interventions. Contemporary enteral-nutrition reviews similarly note that gastric residual volume correlates poorly with aspiration and should not be used as the sole measure of feeding tolerance. Therefore a 350-mL residual without other intolerance findings should be interpreted in the context of the client's overall assessment and local protocol rather than as an automatic stop criterion. B is incorrect because a residual above 200 mL does not by itself establish intolerance or require cessation. C is incorrect because increasing the feeding rate is not an evidence-based response to a moderate residual and could worsen intolerance. D is incorrect because feeding tolerance requires multidimensional clinical assessment rather than reliance on residual volume alone.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Interpret gastric residual volume together with clinical signs of enteral-feeding tolerance and avoid using an isolated residual below 500 mL as an automatic reason to stop enteral nutrition when other intolerance findings are absent.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: removed the absolute-word and answer-length cues, rebuilt all four interpretations to comparable length and specificity, freshly verified current NCBI/Open RN and enteral-nutrition evidence, and preserved overall clinical tolerance rather than an isolated sub-500-mL residual as the single best interpretation.

audit_findings_append.finding: The revised item tests interpretation of a moderate gastric residual with one clearly best evidence-based response, balanced alternatives, and no absolute-word or length cue.

option_audit.A: Correct. It uses the residual in context with the overall tolerance assessment and protocol rather than treating 350 mL as an automatic stop threshold.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. A residual above 200 mL alone does not establish intolerance or require cessation when other clinical signs are absent.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Increasing the feeding rate is not a supported treatment for a moderate residual and may worsen intolerance.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. Residual volume should not replace assessment of gastrointestinal and clinical tolerance findings.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A uniquely reflects the evidence-supported contextual interpretation; B imposes an unsupported threshold, C prescribes an unsafe response, and D ignores clinically relevant tolerance findings.
cueing_check: All four options are parallel clinical interpretations of comparable length and specificity; the prior 'only' distractor and uniquely-long correct response were removed.
